messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] High P95 latency for tenant 'ozora' in dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-ded-3'. Impact: request timeouts and slow completions since 09:12 UTC. Auto-page to #eng-oncall.
Maya: I'm the active on-call, seeing the page. pulling logs now. @Devon can you grab pool metrics and the scheduler dashboard?
Devon: looking — throughput spike on ozora, queue depth up ~3x, lots of 'max_batch_tokens' hits. pod CPU ok, GPU utilization normal. suspect batching knob saturating prefetched tokens.
Samir: any recent deploys or config changes for ozora?
Olga: customer reported an uptick in long responses after their traffic pattern changed at ~09:10 (more short prompts but many parallel). No deploy on our side.
Maya: OK, immediate mitigation options: 1) isolate ozora to a bespoke shaper -> reduce max concurrent batches and lower max_batch_tokens; 2) apply temporary priority bump for other tenants to reduce preemption; 3) enable adaptive batching override (fast-path). Which is least risky?
Devon: fastest is to apply a queue shaper for ozora: set scheduler.knobs.queue_shaper.enabled=true and lower scheduler.knobs.max_batch_tokens to 768 from 2048. That should cut single-batch token budgets and reduce head-of-line blocking.
Samir: +1. Also limit concurrency for ozora to 12 vcpus (tenant concurrency = 12) to prevent queue buildup. We'll revert after stabilization.
Maya: I'll run the change. Pasting the change block — will apply as canary to pool 'eu-west-1-ded-3' only: 
```
PATCH /internal/config/pool/eu-west-1-ded-3/tenants/ozora
{
  "scheduler.knobs.queue_shaper.enabled": "true",
  "scheduler.knobs.max_batch_tokens": "768",
  "tenant.limits.max_concurrency": "12",
  "deployment.note": "temporary mitigations for ozora latency spike - MAYA oncall"
}
```
Maya: applying now (will watch metrics for 1 min).
IncidentBot: Change submitted: config-change-req-9012 by Maya.
Devon: metrics show queue depth starting to fall within 30s, tail latency P95 trending down from 1.8s -> 650ms. No errors so far.
Olga: Ozora support confirms reduced timeouts from customer side. They still see occasional 500s for large prompts.
Samir: For longer prompts, lowering max_batch_tokens can increase fragmentation — may bump token accounting too. If we see cost regressions, consider setting max_batch_tokens = 1024 and enabling prefix KV caching for ozora model variant.
Claire: I'll prepare a quick eval against their prompt set to check quality/regression after the knob change.
Maya: good. I'll keep the config in place for 15m as a canary. After 15m, if stable for 10m, we'll roll to full pool.
Devon: FYI, scheduler logs show a couple of OOM-safe evictions earlier which align with these spikes. No GPU OOMs.
Maya: escalation notes for next shift: if latency returns or queue depth > 2k, escalate to eng-runtime and start tenant isolation (drain other tenants off the same nodes).
Samir: added an alert runbook step: run `scripts/tenant_isolate.sh ozora eu-west-1-ded-3` to create dedicated slice if needed.
Maya: Claire -> results from eval?
Claire: quick local eval shows generation quality unchanged for 95% of tests; a few very long prompts get truncated earlier — we should coordinate with customer to increase their per-request token limit instead of hitting our per-batch cap.
Olga: I'll message the Ozora SRE with suggested transient config and ask them to pause large-batch jobs while we stabilize.
IncidentBot: [NOTICE] config-change-req-9012 applied to canary nodes (4/20).
Devon: P95 now at 480ms and queue depth steady. No new paging.
Maya: holding for stabilization. tagging this thread in runbook: incident-ref 2026-ozora-01.
Samir: once stable, we should add an automatic safeguard: if queue depth spikes with workload skew to many short prompts, auto-decrease max_batch_tokens by 2x for that tenant. Flagging as feature request for Optimize.
Maya: Agree, will open ticket. For now, leaving mitigations in place. Handing off to night oncall @Samir at 10:40 UTC. Please monitor for 1h and revert config when safe.
Samir: taking over. I'll keep the canary running until 11:00 then roll to full pool if stable.
Olga: Ozora SRE confirmed they see normal behavior. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks all, closing my active page.
Samir: acknowledged, marking handoff in PagerDuty.
